narrative:
The model predicts you have a 30% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances of success.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have indicated you do not want to pursue higher education. Among students who passed, every single one expressed a desire to continue studying after school; your lack of that ambition strongly pulls the prediction toward failure. The second most important factor is your clean record of zero past class failures. This actually works in your favor and pushes the outcome toward passing, since it matches the average of students who succeeded. The third notable influence is that you rarely go out with friends. This also nudges the prediction slightly toward passing, as students who limit their social outings tend to have more time available for academics.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on your goals. If you can find motivation to aim for further education, that shift alone could dramatically change your outlook. Consider increasing your weekly study time beyond the two hours you currently spend, since most successful students dedicate more. Even with your good family relationships and low absences, reconnecting with the purpose of your studies will be the most powerful step you can take right now.
